comparison: Perfect agreement on theoretical optical predictions (C23-C25). Both find these standard optical relationships well-supported. OpenEval notes experimental validation in later claims, while peer reviewers acknowledge the NA-based resolution enhancements without challenge.

Strong agreement on background and contextual claims (C7-C14, C89). Both evaluations find these well-supported with appropriate citations. Peer reviewer implicitly acknowledges AMATERAS-1 limitations by noting this work is 'a minor improvement' of previous work.

Significant disagreement on computational sectioning validation (C52-C57, C61). OpenEval finds the method 'clearly explained' with results 'demonstrated in Figure 4D-E' and limitations 'appropriately stated.' Peer reviewers express concern about oversharpening, lack of direct comparisons, and insufficient quantitative validation of axial resolution improvements.

Agreement on data volume claims (C90-C92). Both evaluations find these factual statements about experimental outputs well-supported and consistent with the high-resolution, large-FOV system characteristics.

Disagreement on confocal system implementation (C45-C51). OpenEval finds the design well-documented with 'dramatic background suppression visually demonstrated' and measured PSF characteristics with N=100. Peer reviewers raise concerns about limited use of confocal sectioning in biological samples and request more direct demonstrations of computational sectioning effectiveness.

Partial disagreement on quail embryo experiment (C66-C73, C86-C88). OpenEval finds all experimental parameters 'explicitly stated' and results well-demonstrated. Peer reviewers acknowledge the application but identify critical missing details about volume imaging rate, exposure time, and imaging speed essential for evaluating biological applicability.

Agreement on confocal approach rationale (C40-C42). Both evaluations find the justification for choosing the confocal method well-supported with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this through focus on implementation rather than fundamental method choice.

Agreement on optical specifications (C15-C22, plus system specs C1-C3, C26-C27, C74-C77). Both evaluations confirm these technical specifications are well-documented. Peer reviewers acknowledge the system was 'accomplished' with stated FOV and resolution, and editor describes it as 'important study.'

Agreement on measured PSF characteristics and resolution (C26-C34, C28-C29, C32-C33). Both evaluations support the experimental measurements. OpenEval notes N=100 measurements with error bars; peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge resolution enhancements and provide 'convincing imaging data' assessment.

Agreement on spatial resolution improvements (C78-C81). Both evaluations confirm the measured improvements match theoretical predictions. Peer reviewers acknowledge the enhanced resolution and sensitivity through increased NA without disputing the quantitative claims.

Agreement on brain imaging achievement (C82-C85, C5, C58-C65). Both evaluations support the successful application to mouse brain imaging. Editor notes 'convincing imaging data' and reviewers acknowledge demonstration on brain sections. Concerns about computational sectioning validation exist separately but don't dispute the brain imaging capability itself.

Agreement on mouse brain imaging experiment parameters (C58-C60, C62). Both evaluations find the experimental setup well-documented. OpenEval notes parameters are 'clearly stated'; peer reviewers acknowledge the brain imaging application without disputing these specific claims.

Agreement on cell detection analysis (C63-C65). OpenEval finds the ELEPHANT-based analysis with manual validation of ~640 cells well-supported. Peer reviewers acknowledge the brain imaging results without challenging the cell detection methodology or density calculations.

Partial agreement on quail embryo significance (C86-C88). OpenEval finds the capability demonstrated and novelty claim reasonable. Peer reviewers acknowledge potential for 'long-term imaging of developmental process' but note missing critical details about imaging rates that affect evaluation of biological applicability.

Agreement on quantitative performance metrics (C74-C77). Both evaluations support these calculations based on measured parameters with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers acknowledge the system specifications that underlie these metrics.

Agreement on practical imaging improvements (C36-C39). OpenEval finds the 2× improvement matching theoretical predictions with visual demonstration. Peer reviewers acknowledge resolution enhancements and provide overall positive assessment of imaging data quality.

Agreement on subcellular resolution capability (C39, C80). Both evaluations support the ability to resolve subcellular structures. OpenEval notes sharper features in filamentous actin imaging; peer reviewers implicitly accept this through acknowledgment of resolution improvements.

Agreement on core system specifications (C1-C4). Both evaluations confirm the technical specifications are well-documented. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the 1.5×1.0 cm² FOV and up to 1.2 μm resolution, confirming the system was successfully built.

Agreement on mouse brain application summary (C5). Both evaluations support this abstract claim as validated by detailed results. Editor notes 'convincing imaging data' for mouse brains; OpenEval notes it's demonstrated in Figure 5.

Partial agreement on quail embryo application summary (C6). Both acknowledge the demonstration but peer reviewers identify missing critical details about imaging rates that affect full evaluation of the time-lapse capability claims.
